_README: Additions to the Waypoint Ledger price table, assembled 2026-09-09, so that the table holds the units of care patients actually name. Same law as prices.json: every figure was read out of the cited CMS file or is the product of two figures read in it, with the inputs printed on the face of the coverage statement. Nothing is estimated, inflated, interpolated or recalled. SOURCE FILES, hashed at assembly time: (1) https://www.cms.gov/files/zip/rvu26c-updated-06-30-2026.zip containing PPRRVU2026_Jul_nonQPP.csv — physician fee schedule RVUs and the conversion factor; (2) https://www.cms.gov/files/zip/26clabq3.zip containing PUF_CLFS_CY2026_Q3V1.csv — clinical laboratory fee schedule payment amounts. The conversion factor $33.4009 was READ from the CONV FACTOR column of the RVU file, where it is identical on every line, and it is the same factor the rows already in prices.json use. PFS rows are DERIVED (total non-facility RVU x conversion factor, GPCIs 1.000) and only codes carrying status indicator A on their unmodified line were included. Lab rows are VERIFIED (the payment amount read directly). data/verify_additions.py re-reads both CMS files and recomputes every value_usd in this file.

items.label: Emergency room — the DOCTOR’s half only, level 1 (nurse-level problem)
plain_language_synonyms: emergency room physician fee lowest level
doctor’s bill from the emergency room, minor
items.geography: United States, national (geographic practice cost indices set to 1.000)
items.coverage_statement: The emergency physician’s fee for the least complex emergency department visit — a problem that may not have required a physician at all. HOW THIS NUMBER WAS MADE: CMS does not publish a dollar column in the physician fee schedule. It publishes Relative Value Units and a conversion factor and defines the payment as their product. This figure is 0.33 Total non-facility RVUs x $33.4009 (the CY2026 conversion factor for a non-qualifying APM), at national geographic practice cost indices of 1.000. The RVU total is itself the sum of 0.25 work + 0.05 non-facility practice expense + 0.03 malpractice RVUs, all four figures read in the CMS file on the line for CPT 99281 (status indicator A, active and separately payable). The multiplication is ours, so this is marked DERIVED rather than VERIFIED. You can redo it yourself. This is the emergency physician’s fee only. The hospital bills its own separate emergency department facility fee, which is not in this figure and is usually the larger of the two. Who this describes: people on Medicare fee-for-service — that is, people 65 and older, plus people under 65 who qualified through 24 or more months of disability benefits or who have end-stage kidney disease. Who it does NOT describe: almost everyone this tool is built for. A diagnostic odyssey falls hardest on working-age adults, who are overwhelmingly on employer coverage, a Marketplace plan, Medicaid, or uninsured — and none of those prices are in this figure. Read it as a PRICE FLOOR, not as your bill: commercial insurance normally pays more than Medicare, and an uninsured person is billed the provider’s charge instead, which is routinely several times this amount.

Who it does NOT describe: if you have private insurance you pay your deductible and then coinsurance on a negotiated rate that is normally higher than this one; if you are uninsured you are billed the laboratory’s charge, which for common tests runs several times this rate. Read it as a PRICE FLOOR, not as your bill.
